en: 'Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to us; they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Burayd narrated to me, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: News of the departure of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reached us while we were in Yemen, so we set out migrating to him—I and two brothers of mine, I being the youngest of the two, one of them Abu Burdah and the other Abu Ruhm—with either—he said—over fifty, or fifty-three, or fifty-two men of my people. He said: We boarded a boat, but our boat cast us ashore with the Negus in Abyssinia, where we met Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions with him. Ja'far said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent us here and commanded us to stay, so stay with us.' So we stayed with him until we all arrived together. He said: We met the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) right when he had conquered Khaybar, so he assigned a share for us—or he said: gave us from it. And he did not distribute anything from it to anyone who was absent from the conquest of Khaybar except for those who were present with him, except for the companions of our boat along with Ja'far and his companions, for whom he apportioned shares along with them. He said: Some people used to say to us—meaning to the people of the boat: 'We preceded you in migration.' He said: Then Asma' bint 'Umays—and she was among those who had arrived with us—entered upon Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), visiting her, and she had migrated to the Negus among those who migrated to him. 'Umar entered upon Hafsah while Asma' was with her, and when 'Umar saw Asma', he said: 'Who is this?' She said: 'Asma' bint 'Umays.' 'Umar said: 'Is this the Abyssinian one? Is this the seafarer?' Asma' said: 'Yes.' 'Umar said: 'We preceded you in migration, so we have more right to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) than you!' At that, she became angry and said a word: 'You have spoken falsely, O 'Umar! No, by Allah! You were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who fed your hungry and instructed your ignorant, while we were in the abode—or in the land—of the distant, hostile foreigners in Abyssinia, and that was for the sake of Allah and His Messenger! By Allah, I will neither taste food nor drink anything until I mention what you said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). We were harmed and frightened, and I will surely mention that to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and ask him. By Allah, I will not lie, nor deviate, nor add anything to that!' He said: When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived, she said: 'O Prophet of Allah, 'Umar said such and such.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'He does not have more right to me than you do; he and his companions have a single migration, while you, the people of the boat, have two migrations.' She said: 'And indeed I saw Abu Musa and the companions of the boat coming to me in groups, asking me about this hadith; there was nothing in the world that made them happier or was greater in their souls than what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to them.' Abu Burdah said: Asma' said: 'And indeed I saw Abu Musa repeatedly asking me to recount this hadith.'
